title: United Express 5925

location.name: Quincy Municipal Airport runway intersection, Illinois

summary: United Express Flight 5925 collided with King Air A90 at runway intersection during landing/takeoff. King Air pilots failed to effectively monitor CTAF and scan for traffic. Cherokee pilot's interrupted transmission led United Express crew to misunderstand King Air's intentions. Post-crash fire killed all 14 occupants on both aircraft.
probable_cause: The failure of the pilots in the King Air A90 to effectively monitor the common traffic advisory frequency or to properly scan for traffic, resulting in their commencing a takeoff roll when the Beech 1900C was landing on an intersecting runway. Contributing to the cause was the Cherokee pilot's interrupted radio transmission, which led to the Beech 1900C pilots' misunderstanding of the transmission as an indication from the King Air that it would not take off until after flight 5925 had cleared the runway. Contributing to the severity of the accident and loss of life were the lack of adequate aircraft rescue and fire fighting services, and the failure of the air stair door on the Beech 1900C to open. (p. 79)

factors.evidence: King Air pilots failed to effectively monitor common traffic advisory frequency or properly scan for traffic (p. 79)
Cherokee pilot's interrupted radio transmission blocked clear reception and led Beech 1900C pilots to misunderstand message (p. 79)
King Air began takeoff roll when Flight 5925 was landing on intersecting runway at 1700:59 (p. 27)
Fire enveloped both aircraft quickly, lack of adequate ARFF contributed to fatalities (p. 78)

events.text: Flight 5925 departed Chicago O'Hare with 10 passengers plus crew (p. 26)
Made intermediate stop at Burlington, Iowa (p. 26)
Captain at 1652:07 announced on CTAF about 30 miles north, landing runway 13, requested any traffic advise (p. 26)
At 1655:19 King Air announced taxiing out takeoff runway 04. At 1655:40 Cherokee announced back-taxi to runway 04 (p. 26)
Captain at 1655:48 commented both using runway 04, confirmed plan runway 13 (p. 26)
At 1656:56 captain announced on CTAF 10 miles north, left base runway 13 (p. 26)
At 1659:03 King Air announced holding short runway 04, taking runway, heading southeast (p. 26-27)
At 1659:29 captain announced 6 mile final runway 13 (p. 27)
At 1700:16 captain asked if King Air would hold or take off, requested King Air intentions (p. 27)
At 1700:28 Cherokee pilot responded holding runway 04. GPWS gave 200 feet alert interrupting transmission (p. 27)
Flight 5925 touched down on runway 13 at 1700:59. King Air began takeoff roll about 13 seconds earlier (p. 27-28)
Aircraft collided at runway intersection, skidded and caught fire (p. 28)
Rescuers heard signs of life in Beech 1900C but could not open air stair door due to fuselage deformation (p. 28)

recommendations.text: Reiterate to flight instructors the importance of emphasizing careful scanning techniques during pilot training and biennial flight reviews
Evaluate the propensity of the Beech 1900C door/frame system to jam when it sustains minimal permanent door deformation and require appropriate design changes
Establish clear and specific methods for showing compliance with freedom from jamming certification requirements
Consider Quincy accident circumstances when developing methods for showing compliance with freedom from jamming requirements
Review and improve guidance for principal maintenance inspectors to ensure maintenance personnel properly trained
Develop ways to fund airports served by scheduled passenger operations and require ARFF units during commuter flight operations
Add to Safety Information Section of FAA Internet Home Page list of airports with scheduled air service but without aircraft rescue and fire fighting capabilities
